title: Product basis
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\{b_i:i\in I\}$ is a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$, with one basis vector constant one, and that the basis is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For each natural number $n$, the product functions $x\mapsto\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}b_{a(j)}(x(j))$, indexed by all maps $a:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to I$, form a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega^n$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function basis indexed by $I$
The basis has a constant-one vector
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
